function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

A **mandate** is a formal, written instruction that authorises a third‑party (usually a bank, payment service provider, or other financial institution) to act on behalf of a client. In practice it’s the legal basis that lets the third‑party perform specific actions—such as initiating payments, collecting funds, or managing a financial account—without the client having to intervene each time. ### Key points | Aspect | What it means | |--------|---------------| | **Purpose** | Gives a service provider the right to execute transactions or manage funds for a client. | | **Typical use cases** | • Direct debit authorisations (e.g., utility bills, subscription services)
• Standing orders
• Automated payment collections for payroll or rent | | **Legal nature** | A signed agreement (often electronic) that complies with local regulations (e.g., PSD2 in the EU). | | **Lifecycle** | • **Pending** – the mandate has been created but not yet activated (e.g., awaiting client signature).
• **Active** – fully authorised; the provider can now act on the client’s behalf.
• **Inactive** – cancelled, expired, or revoked. | ### In the context of the API you’re working with - **`user_mandates`**: Retrieves mandates that belong to a specific client (identified by their full name). You can filter by status (`active`, `pending`, `inactive`) or get all of them if you omit the status. - **`partner_mandates`**: Retrieves mandates that belong to the partner’s entire client base. Again, you can filter by status or fetch all. These endpoints let partners (e.g., fintech platforms) programmatically inspect the state of the mandates they’ve issued to their users, which is essential for compliance, reporting, and operational workflows. --- #### Quick example ```python # Get all active mandates for a particular client mandates = user_mandates(name="Jane Doe", status="active") ``` This call would return a list of mandate objects that Jane Doe has authorised and that are currently active. Feel free to ask if you’d like more detail on any specific part—such as how mandates are created, how they’re stored, or how to handle status transitions!
